# Things to do and places to visit in Anglesey

A warm welcome and a busy time are guaranteed for visitors to Ynys Môn (Anglesey). For a small island it packs in a heck of a lot. With so many options for brilliant Ynys Môn days out, we've chosen ten favourites to get you started.

SaveShare

With so much to see and do on Ynys Môn, a beautiful [National Landscape](https://national-landscapes.org.uk/national-landscapes/anglesey), you’d be forgiven for not knowing where to start. Scroll our must‑do list for inspiration, or jump straight to the section that interests you most; whether you’re exploring [standout attractions](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/isle-anglesey/ten-things-do-anglesey#Attractions), discovering stunning [beaches](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/isle-anglesey/ten-things-do-anglesey#Beaches), delving into the island’s [rich heritage](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/isle-anglesey/ten-things-do-anglesey#Heritage), or looking for [upcoming events](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/north-wales/isle-anglesey/ten-things-do-anglesey#Events), you’ll find everything you need below.

## Anglesey attractions

### The Menai Suspension Bridge

It’s unlikely you'll miss this Ynys Môn highlight, the Menai Suspension Bridge. Chances are you're drive across it.

Built by Thomas Telford and opened in 1826, it’s the first modern suspension bridge in the world and it connects the mainland to [Menai Bridge](https://www.visitanglesey.co.uk/en-gb/explore/towns/menai-bridge) \- one of the five towns in Ynys Môn. Prior to its construction, cattle farmers would somehow have to persuade their herd to swim across the Menai Strait to market. Discover more about the bridge's history at the [Menai Bridge Community Heritage Trust's](https://www.visitwales.com/product/912727) museum.

![Suspension bridge with houses and trees in the distance, and a rib boat on the Menai Strait](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_fullbleed__thin_1x/public/media-library/2025-01/25061-menai-straits-anglesey-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=lmIbzw2H)

### Isle of Anglesey Coastal Path

There are countless places worth visiting along the 140 mile/ 225 km [Anglesey Coastal Path](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2168930). It goes right round the island with some sections doubling as a cycle route and bridleway. The Friends of the Isle of Anglesey Coast Path website has handy [maps and detailed descriptions of the path's 12 sections](https://sites.google.com/site/friendsofangleseycoastalpath/home), and once you’ve made it all the way round, you can claim a badge and a certificate.

As well as skirting the spectacular coastline, the path passes through farmland, coastal heath, dunes and small pockets of woodland. Highlights include South Stack lighthouse, the sea arches at Bwa Gwyn and the wild flowers and birdlife at Aberffraw dunes.

![A person on a stone bridge looking towards a beach.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2025-08/WCP_ROBIN%20ANGLESEY%208.jpg.webp?itok=ODKBJ3tv)

### Llanddwyn Island

This romantic outcrop extending from the mainland is one of the most picturesque locations in Wales.

The ruined church was once home to Saint Dwynwen - the Welsh patron saint of lovers from the 5th century AD. When her true love Maelon was turned to ice, Dwynwen had the good sense to move to Llanddwyn Island - and probably didn’t regret it for a minute. [Llanddwyn beach](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1821332) is a cosy cove of pristine sand and it's backed by a forest that's home to rare red squirrels. So, forget St Valentine! Here in Wales we celebrate all things to do with love on [St Dwynwen's Day](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3318) on 25 January.

![Image of the lighthouse and beach at Ynys Llanddwyn in the bright winter sun.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2021-01/NVW-C158-1819-0003.jpg.webp?itok=v2mSg8EG)

### Parys Mountain

There are surprises around every corner in Ynys Môn, with one of them being [Parys Mountain](https://www.visitanglesey.co.uk/en-gb/explore/landscape/parys-mountain) in Amlwch - once the largest copper mine in the world.

The unique landscape of Parys Mountain has to be seen to be believed: a dramatic sweep of peaks and troughs, coloured in every shade of yellow, brown and orange imaginable.

In the 18th century, people travelled from across the UK to dig for copper, sparking what became known as the Welsh Copper Rush. Today, this is an open‑access landscape attraction, and visitors are still welcome to walk the site and explore its remarkable terrain.

![A vivid view of Parys Mountain’s colourful open‑cast landscape, showing rugged yellow, orange and brown slopes surrounding a deep blue water pool, with the historic windmill tower visible on the ridge beneath a bright blue sky.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_small__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2026-03/53696-nvw-e14-2122-0471-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=LeJeeHeD)

Parys Mountain, Ynys Môn, North Wales

### South Stack Lighthouse

[South Stack](https://www.visitwales.com/product/752538) lighthouse perches on its own tiny island off the far western edge of the Welsh coast.

Just getting there is a real adventure (and probably not a good idea if you suffer from vertigo). It's reached via 400 steps in the cliffside and a bridge high above the roaring waves. Visitors can tour the engine room and then climb the narrow stairs right to the top for epic views out to sea.

The birdwatching all around here is spectacular; you’ll soon be playing the time-honoured game of spot-the-puffin. If you're really lucky, you might even see one of the rare breeding pairs of choughs among the colonies of guillemots and razorbills clinging to the cliffs.

Read more about [visiting lighthouses in Wales](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3156).

![lighthouse on grassy outcrop.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2020-05/NVW-D12-2021-0005-small.jpg.webp?itok=O2KTyKhi)

South Stack Lighthouse, Ynys Môn, North Wales

### Plas Newydd House and Gardens

Situated on the shore of the Menai Strait, [Plas Newydd House and Gardens](https://www.visitwales.com/product/958715) was once the home of the Marquess of Ynys Môn and dates back to the 18th century.

Now managed by the National Trust, it's a feast of ornate Neo-classical rooms, many with intricate wallpaper and fabrics. And it's packed with unusual furnishings. Perhaps the most remarkable exhibit is a vast mural painted by artist Rex Whistler who was a regular visitor to the house in the early 20th century. Outside there are gardens with panoramic views across the Menai Strait towards the mountains of Eryri - and also an Australian arboretum.

![Country estate manor on the edge of the water](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2022-11/NVW-C158-1819-0095.jpg.webp?itok=XvB54z3s)

Plas Newydd House and Gardens, Ynys Môn, North Wales

View Credits

### The Dingle Nature Reserve

If you’re looking for kingfishers, woodpeckers and moorhens, this is the place.

The [Dingle Nature Reserve](https://www.visitanglesey.co.uk/en-gb/explore/wildlife/dingle-local-nature-reserve) is an ancient 25-acre wooded valley. It's a tranquil hideaway carpeted with bluebells in spring and home to all manner of wildlife. Footbridges, walkways and benches have been installed to make it easier to enjoy the Cefni river as it chortles its way through the trees. Keep an eye out for the sculptures by local artists including a dragonfly and giant seed pods.

### Halen Môn sea salt

Ynys Môn is also home to the innovative food production business [Halen Môn](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1926152), producer of pure Welsh sea salt enjoyed by chefs and food lovers around the world. Their sea salt can also be found in many delicatessens nationwide, and you can purchase some of the unique sea salt flavours at the on-site shop, including local produce and artisan gifts. All visitors can also take a behind-the-scenes tour of the Salt Cote or embrace the outdoor [wild seaweed bath experience](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2172530).

### Anglesey beaches

It's hard to choose a favourite, but [Lligwy Beach](https://www.thebeachguide.co.uk/north-wales/anglesey/traeth-lligwy.htm) is one of the nicest - a wide sheltered bay on the North East coast. The shore here shelves really gently and the water is shallow. There's plenty of golden sand too, so it's ideal for families with kids. Offshore you might spot seals and dolphins and the consistent breezes mean it's also popular with wind and kite-surfers.

[Llanddwyn Beach](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1821332), with its impressive sand dunes and beautiful coves, offers stunning views of Eryri and Pen Llŷn (Llŷn Peninsula). The Tŵr Mawr lighthouse provides a prime spot for wildlife watching, including seals, dolphins, and occasionally minke whales. It’s an ideal picnic location in good weather and a place of natural beauty that is especially striking during the winter months.

[Benllech](https://www.visitwales.com/twg-product/528811) is one of the most popular beaches on Ynys Môn. It has miles of golden sand and clear blue waters. People love sunbathing on the flat beach before having a paddle or trying stand up paddleboards (SUP) in the waters. It is accessible to those with wheelchairs or pushchairs and is very family friendly.

![A narrow paved path leads downhill toward a calm bay, with rocky cliffs and green grassy slopes on either side. Sunlight highlights the golden cliffs in the distance under a cloudy sky.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__portrait__1_1x/public/media-library/2026-01/Portth%20Swtan.jpg.webp?itok=1-g4QUA9)

[Beaumaris Beach](https://www.gonorthwales.co.uk/things-to-do/beaumaris-beach-p376811) straddles Beaumaris Pier and is known as a hotspot for yachting and the boarding point for boat trips to Puffin Island. It is part of the [Anglesey Coastal Path](https://www.visitanglesey.co.uk/en/about-anglesey/isle-of-anglesey-coastal-path/) (which is well worth exploring) and has panoramic views across the Menai Strait to Bangor, Eryri and Llandudno’s Great Orme.

For a more rural hideaway, visit [Porth Swtan (Church Bay)](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1821176), an unspoilt sand and pebble beach. Accessed via a steep footpath from Porth Swtan / Church Bay village, it feels hidden away from the crowds. Clamber along the rock pools, go swimming, fish or surf to make the most of the natural beauty.

If you’re after a wide beach with plenty of opportunities for activity, try [Porth Dafarch](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1821175), a sandy cove between Trearddur Bay and Holyhead. It’s a cycle-friendly beach with a slipway ramp and is popular with canoeists, SUPers and divers as well as families.

You can hire stand up paddleboards (SUP), canoes and other watersports equipment from [B-Active](https://www.visitwales.com/product/923265) in Rhoscolyn, and [FunSport](https://www.funsportonline.co.uk/rentals/) or [Gecko](http://www.geckosurf.co.uk/equipment-hire/) in Rhosneigr.

Find out more about the lovely [beaches in North Wales](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3263).

### Anglesey's heritage attractions

Wales is home to literally hundreds of castles, but without question [Castell Biwmares (Beaumaris Castle)](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2003622) is one of the best - a massive fortress of almost perfect symmetry. The last great castle built, but never completed, under Edward I in the 13th century. At the time it was at the cutting edge of castle design. Lack of money and trouble keeping the quarrelsome Scots under control meant the south gatehouse and six great towers never reached their intended heights. Don’t for a moment let that put you off visiting though - there are plenty of spooky corridors and narrow spiral staircases just waiting to be explored.

The island was considered holy by the Celts; it was a stronghold of their priests, the Druids, who planted it with groves of sacred oaks. This was the last pocket of Wales to resist the Roman invasion in the first century AD. For the advancing army, the island’s rich copper reserves were well worth the fight. Before that, Môn had been home to Neolithic and Bronze Age communities, whose burial mounds remain. The [Prehistoric Monuments of Anglesey](https://www.anglesey-history.co.uk/places/prehistoric-monuments/) website lists several sites you can visit, including [Bryn Celli Ddu](https://www.visitwales.com/twg-product/530641), [Barclodiad y Gawres](https://www.visitwales.com/twg-product/528051) and [Presaddfed](https://cadw.gov.wales/visit/places-to-visit/presaddfed-chambered-tomb) chambered tombs.

## What’s on in Ynys Môn?

There's normally a packed calendar of events taking place on the island. There are food festivals, agricultural shows, children's events, music performances and fairs - particularly in spring and summer months.

**May/June:** [Gottwood Festival](https://www.gottwood.co.uk/) – a boutique electronic music and arts festival set in the magical woodland of Carreglwyd Estate. Expect an eclectic mix of world‑class DJs, immersive art installations and a laid‑back, friendly vibe in an unforgettable natural setting.

**August:** [Tour de Môn](https://alwaysaimhighevents.com/events/tour-de-mon-2026) – a much‑loved cycling event that attracts riders from across the UK. The route showcases Ynys Môn's spectacular coastline, peaceful villages and iconic landmarks. With multiple distances available, it’s suitable for cyclists of all abilities and a brilliant way to experience the island’s natural beauty.

To keep up to date with the latest developments for what's on check the [Visit Anglesey website](https://www.visitanglesey.co.uk/en-gb).

## Towns and villages worth exploring

Discover the character and charm of Ynys Môn beyond its coastline. From colourful harbours to historic market squares, these villages and towns offer a mix of culture, local flavours, and stunning scenery. Perfect for a leisurely stroll, a bite to eat, or simply soaking up the island’s unique atmosphere.
